items.actClause: AN ACT in relation to authorizing school buses and paratransit vehicles types A(I) and A(II) used solely for the transportation of children or people with disabilities to travel on parkways
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5844

TITLE OF BILL:  An act in relation to authorizing school buses and
paratransit vehicles types A(I) and A(II) used solely for the
transportation of children or people with disabilities to travel on
parkways

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

to allow small school buses and paratransit vehicles types A(I) and
A(II) to travel on state parkways when transporting children or people
with disabilities.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill authorizes school buses and paratransit
vehicles type A(I) and A(II) to travel state parkways when
transporting children with disabilities or children.

Section 2. Effective Date.

JUSTIFICATION:

The State's parkway system originally was created to provide a scenic
way into, or out of, and around New York City. But today, the state
parkways are for the most part equivalent to expressways, except for a
few oddities, such as low, stone-arch overpasses that would trap
trucks, commercial vehicles and tractor trailers, which is why they
are banned from parkways.

Due to the parkways' banning of commercial vehicles, trucks, and
tractor trailers, mini school buses and paratransit buses, type A(I)
and A(II), which clear these overpasses, are banned from traveling the
parkways. Often times these vehicles are transporting children and
people with disabilities. Banning these vehicles from parkways, in
cases when transporting children and people with disabilities, can
often times double the commute times for these groups.

This legislation would allow for these specific types of vehicles to
travel on the state's parkways while transporting children and people
with disabilities. These populations suffer the most by the lengthy
travel times they are subjected to by not allowing mini school buses
and paratransit vehicles to travel the parkways.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately.
